title: Veneto
description: Venice's hinterland: Amarone from dried grapes, Soave from volcanic hills and Prosecco from steep slopes.
L: From the Alps to the lagoon

The Veneto, in north-east Italy, runs from the Dolomites and the Lessini mountains down to the plains and the Venetian lagoon. Lake Garda borders it on the west. Key areas: Valpolicella and Soave, near Verona; Conegliano and Valdobbiadene, north of Venice, for Prosecco.

The climate is moderate continental, with warm summers and cold winters. Lake Garda moderates the west, and the Alps protect from northern winds. Hillsides give cooler nights and better drainage than the fertile, flat plains, where much simple wine is made.
Hills for quality, plains for volume
Why do the Veneto's best wines come from hills?
Hills give freshness and drainage; plains favour volume.

The Veneto is Italy's largest wine region by volume, thanks to Prosecco and Pinot Grigio. But it also makes some of Italy's most distinctive wines. Venice's merchants traded wine for centuries, and the tradition of drying grapes, appassimento, has ancient roots here.
The Veneto is Italy's largest wine region by volume.
Yes, thanks largely to Prosecco and Pinot Grigio.
The Veneto runs from the Alps to the Venetian lagoon
Hills give its best wines; plains give volume
It's Italy's largest wine region by volume

Corvina is the main grape of Valpolicella and Bardolino, giving sour cherry and almond, with thick skins ideal for drying. Corvinone, a separate, larger-berried grape, and Rondinella, which adds colour, are its partners. Molinara was once common; Oseleta is being revived.

Garganega makes Soave, with lemon, almond and minerality. Glera makes Prosecco, light and floral. Turbiana makes Lugana on Lake Garda. The Veneto also produces huge amounts of Pinot Grigio, mostly under the Delle Venezie DOC, and international grapes like Merlot and Chardonnay.
Match each grape to its wine.
Native grapes make the Veneto's signature wines.
Look for Lugana, from Turbiana on Lake Garda's southern shore. It's a textured, age-worthy white, less known than Soave.
Which grape is the backbone of Valpolicella?
Corvina, Corvinone and Rondinella make Valpolicella
Garganega makes Soave; Glera makes Prosecco
The Veneto also makes lots of Pinot Grigio

Valpolicella lies north of Verona, in valleys running down from the Lessini mountains. The Classico zone, around Fumane, Marano and Negrar, is the historic heart. Simple Valpolicella is light and cherry-fresh. Superiore has more alcohol and ageing.

For Amarone and Recioto, the best bunches are dried for about 100 to 120 days in airy lofts, fruttai, losing 30 to 40% of their weight. Recioto della Valpolicella ferments sweet. Amarone della Valpolicella, DOCG since 2010, ferments nearly dry, to 15 to 16% alcohol, with dried cherry, raisin, chocolate and spice. It ages at least two years.
From dried grapes fermented nearly dry
Appassimento concentrates the grapes; fermentation runs almost dry.

Ripasso, re-passed, is Valpolicella refermented on the leftover skins of Amarone or Recioto, gaining body, colour and dried fruit flavour. It's sometimes called baby Amarone, sitting between simple Valpolicella and Amarone in weight and price.
Which Valpolicella wines use dried grapes or their skins?
Amarone and Recioto use dried grapes: dry and sweet
Ripasso is refermented on Amarone skins

Soave lies east of Verona. Soave Classico, in the hills around Soave and Monteforte d'Alpone, has volcanic basalt and limestone soils. Soave must be at least 70% Garganega, with Trebbiano di Soave or Chardonnay. Vines are traditionally trained on pergolas, pergola veronese.

Soave was mass-produced in the 1970s, earning a poor reputation. Producers like Pieropan and Inama showed its real potential: mineral, almond-scented, age-worthy wines. Soave Superiore DOCG requires lower yields. Since 2019, 33 UGAs, named sub-areas like Foscarino and Calvarino, can appear on labels.
What must Soave contain at least 70% of?

Recioto di Soave, DOCG since 1998, is a sweet wine from dried Garganega. Grapes dry for months, concentrating sugar, sometimes with noble rot. The wine is golden, honeyed and sweet, with apricot and almond, balanced by acidity.
Recioto di Soave is a sweet wine made from dried grapes.
Soave Classico grows Garganega on volcanic hills
Quality rose from cheap volume to named sub-areas
Recioto di Soave is sweet, from dried grapes

Prosecco DOC covers nine provinces in the Veneto and Friuli, mostly on flat land, making large volumes; at least 85% Glera. Two DOCGs are on hills: Conegliano Valdobbiadene Prosecco Superiore, north of Treviso, and Asolo. The grape was renamed from Prosecco to Glera in 2009, to protect the place name.
DOC on plains, DOCG on hills

Most Prosecco is made by the tank method, also called Martinotti or Charmat: the second fermentation happens in a sealed, pressurised tank. This keeps Glera's fresh pear, apple and floral aromas, without the bready notes of long lees ageing. It's faster and cheaper than the traditional method.
Match each Prosecco term to its meaning.

Conegliano Valdobbiadene's steep hills, a UNESCO site since 2019, are worked mostly by hand. Rive are 43 single-village crus. Cartizze, a 107-hectare hill near Valdobbiadene, is the most prized. Hill wines are more aromatic and complex than those from the plains.
Why was the Prosecco grape renamed Glera?
To protect Prosecco as a place name
A grape can grow anywhere; a protected place name can't be copied.
Prosecco DOC is large; Conegliano Valdobbiadene and Asolo are hill DOCGs
The tank method keeps Glera's fruit fresh
Rive and Cartizze are the hills' top crus
Reading the Veneto and eating with it

Labels show DOC or DOCG, like Amarone della Valpolicella or Soave Classico, plus Classico for the historic zone, Superiore for higher ripeness or ageing, and Ripasso. For Prosecco, look for Superiore, Rive or Cartizze, and the sweetness: Brut, Extra Dry, which is sweeter than Brut, and Dry.

Valpolicella suits salumi and pasta; Ripasso suits risotto and roasts; Amarone suits braised beef, game and aged cheese, and flavours risotto all'Amarone. Soave suits risotto, seafood and antipasti. Prosecco suits cicchetti, Venetian small bites, and makes the Spritz and the Bellini. Recioto suits pandoro.
Which cocktail uses Prosecco and white peach?
In Venice, a glass of Prosecco with cicchetti at a bàcaro, a small wine bar, is the local way to start an evening.
